issues.title: Narrowing recovered_open silently drops the 'escalation open' badge for insufficient_data / grandfathered / unjudged rows
issues.description:
`_parity`'s docstring asserts "Every pre-existing name is preserved verbatim; the change is purely additive for existing consumers." The names are preserved, but `recovered_open` is NARROWED to the `no_alarm` verdict, and the existing consumer branches on the name, not on the semantics.

`dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/tab_memory_evals.jsx::verdictBadge` (on main as of dec8c9f4, 2026-08-01 21:26 — i.e. it landed AFTER this branch's base e1c04cf3, so it is absent from this worktree and no test in this branch can catch the regression) branches on exactly three parity values: `recovered_open`, `alarmed_unlinked`, `storm_collapsed`; everything else falls through to the plain verdict badge. Its own comment documents the old behaviour explicitly: "`recovered_open` is derived for EVERY non-alarm verdict that carries a linked escalation ... `insufficient_data`, `grandfathered` and a null verdict all reach it."

After this change those rows emit `insufficient_data_open` / `grandfathered_open` / `unjudged_open` / `unknown_verdict_open`, none of which the JSX knows, so the badge silently degrades from `badge warn` "insufficient_data · escalation open" to `badge muted` "insufficient_data". The producer became more precise and the UI became less informative — a silent degradation, against the module's own loud-over-silent rule. (The `EscalationLink` chip is driven by `m.escalation`, not parity, so the link itself survives; it is the warn-level badge refinement that is lost.) `unknown_verdict` additionally renders identically to an absent verdict ('no verdict', muted), erasing the distinction the new state exists to draw.

Fix: either extend the JSX to a suffix-aware `_open` check (e.g. `parity.endsWith('_open')` → warn + '· escalation open') plus an `unknown_verdict` label, in the same commit; or drop the claim of pure additivity and file the UI follow-up as a blocking dependency of this landing.
issues.failure_scenario: A metric with verdict `insufficient_data` (or `grandfathered`, or no verdict entry) has a linked open eval_regression escalation. Before: parity `recovered_open` → tab renders `badge warn` reading 'insufficient_data · escalation open'. After this change: parity `insufficient_data_open` → `verdictBadge` matches no branch → renders plain `badge muted` 'insufficient_data'. The operator loses the visual signal that an escalation is open on a metric that was never successfully judged.
issues.suggestion: Update tab_memory_evals.jsx's verdictBadge in the same change (suffix-aware `_open` handling + an `unknown_verdict` label), or gate this landing on the UI follow-up and correct the 'purely additive for existing consumers' claim in _parity's docstring.

issues.title: internal_error in _UNCACHEABLE_ISSUE_KINDS can permanently defeat the memory-evals cache — the failure mode this change rejects elsewhere
issues.description:
`_UNCACHEABLE_ISSUE_KINDS` includes `internal_error`, and `root_scan_succeeded` returns False whenever one is present. `root_scan_succeeded`'s docstring justifies this with "a bug is never a steady state — it is an emergency with no known trigger — so the walk it costs is bounded by how long the bug lives."

Both halves of that argument are weaker than stated:

1. The per-eval `internal_error` raised from `_build_payload`'s new per-eval loop does NOT abort the build (the docstring says "a bug aborted the build, so the payload is missing rows"). It drops one row and the rest of the payload is complete and useful — exactly the "completed over a degraded tree" case the same predicate deliberately keeps cacheable.
2. A bug reachable from artifact CONTENT is deterministic and recurs on every single build, so it is a steady state until someone deploys a fix. That is precisely the "permanent property of a corrupt file ... would defeat the cache forever in front of the very walk it protects" argument this change uses to reject `parse_failures` and `archives_present` as predicates.

The same commit makes such a bug strictly more reachable: `_ARTIFACT_ERRORS` no longer catches `TypeError`/`AttributeError`, so any artifact shape not covered by an existing isinstance guard now escapes as `internal_error` instead of degrading one row. (`json.loads` on deeply-nested input raising `RecursionError` is another artifact-caused, non-ValueError path.)

At minimum the docstring should stop claiming the bug aborted the build; better, treat the per-eval `internal_error` (build completed, one row lost) as cacheable and reserve uncacheability for the top-level guard's `internal_error` (build genuinely aborted) — the two are already distinguishable by whether `eval_id` is set on the issue.
issues.failure_scenario: A `metrics-*.json` artifact contains a shape not covered by an existing isinstance guard, so `_build_eval` raises TypeError. `_build_payload` records a per-eval `internal_error`; the other nine evals build fine. `root_scan_succeeded` now returns False on every build, so the 60s TTL never stores anything and every 3s dashboard poll re-runs the full tree walk plus the escalation-queue index — for as long as the artifact sits on disk, which is indefinitely.
issues.suggestion: Distinguish the aborting top-level internal_error from the per-eval one (the latter carries eval_id) and keep the per-eval case cacheable; and correct root_scan_succeeded's docstring, which currently describes only the aborting case.

issues.title: archives_present is documented as the operator-facing diagnostic but has no consumer
issues.description:
`archives_present` is described in three separate docstrings (build_escalation_analytics, archive_scan_succeeded, api_escalation_analytics) and in TestArchivesPresent as "the completeness DIAGNOSTIC an operator reads" / "An operator reads it to find a root that is unmounted or misconfigured". Nothing reads it: `grep -rn 'archives_present\|archivesPresent' dashboard/src/dashboard/static/ dashboard/tests/js/` returns no hits, and no Python test asserts it is surfaced.

As shipped, only `archives_reached` has a consumer (the cache gate). The stated operator-facing purpose of `archives_present` is unrealized, so an unmounted or misconfigured archive root still renders as an ordinary empty project panel with no signal — which is the condition the field was introduced to make visible, and which the module's loud-over-silent norm says must not be silent.
issues.failure_scenario: A project root's data/escalations volume fails to mount. build_escalation_analytics sets archives_present: false, the payload is still cached (archives_reached is true from the other roots), and the Escalation Analytics tab renders that project with zero filings and no indication anything is wrong — identical to a project that has genuinely never escalated.
issues.suggestion: Either render archives_present in tab_escalation_analytics.jsx (a banner naming the unreached roots), or narrow the docstrings to say it is a payload field awaiting a UI consumer and file the follow-up. Carrying the per-root labels rather than a bare bool would make the banner actionable.

verdict.summary: The change is careful, well-tested (176 dashboard tests pass locally) and the two cache predicates are correctly reasoned: `archives_reached` (any) vs `archives_present` (all) is the right split, `_ARTIFACT_ERRORS` narrowing to `(OSError, ValueError)` is sound for `_load_json` (JSONDecodeError and UnicodeDecodeError are both ValueError subclasses; `Path.is_dir` swallows OSError so the `OSError`-only walk catch is right), the `_index_escalations` narrowing is genuinely protected by the pre-existing `isinstance(status, str)` guard, and `_verdict_class` correctly does isinstance-before-frozenset. `_parity` stays total and `PARITY_STATES` matches the reachable outputs. Three issues remain. The significant one is cross-layer: `_parity`'s docstring claims the change is "purely additive for existing consumers", but narrowing `recovered_open` to the `no_alarm` verdict silently strips the "· escalation open" warn badge from `insufficient_data` / `grandfathered` / unjudged rows in `tab_memory_evals.jsx`, which landed on main after this branch's base and is therefore not visible to this branch's tests. Second, `internal_error` in `_UNCACHEABLE_ISSUE_KINDS` makes a deterministic, data-triggered bug permanently defeat the memory-evals TTL cache — the exact failure mode the same change explicitly rejects for `parse_failures` and `archives_present` — and the narrowing of `_ARTIFACT_ERRORS` makes such a bug more reachable. Third, `archives_present` is documented in three places as the diagnostic "an operator reads" but has no consumer anywhere in the UI or JS tests.
